scheme_name: Assistance for Cattleshed, Gaman, Water Tank and Bucket
description:
The Assistance for Cattleshed, Gaman, Water Tank and Bucket scheme is a welfare initiative launched by the Government of India to support farmers and livestock owners in enhancing their agricultural productivity and improving their living conditions.

This scheme was officially launched in the year 2020 as part of the broader efforts to strengthen rural livelihoods and promote sustainable agricultural practices.

The primary objective of the scheme is to provide financial assistance for the construction of cattle sheds and water tanks, as well as the provision of buckets for water storage.

The scheme aims to improve the living conditions of livestock by ensuring that they have proper shelter and access to clean water.

The government has set a target of constructing over 1 million cattle sheds across various states by the end of the financial year 2024.

The financial assistance provided under this scheme is substantial.

Eligible beneficiaries can receive up to ₹50,000 for the construction of a cattleshed.

In addition, the scheme provides ₹10,000 for the construction of a water tank.

Farmers can also receive ₹1,000 for the purchase of buckets for water storage.

The total potential financial assistance for a single beneficiary can reach up to ₹61,000.

Eligibility criteria for this scheme are clearly defined to ensure that the assistance reaches the intended beneficiaries.

Farmers must be registered with the local agricultural department to qualify for the benefits.

The age limit for applicants is set at a minimum of 18 years.

There is no upper age limit specified for applicants.

Income criteria are also established, where the annual income of the applicant should not exceed ₹2 lakh.

This income limit is aimed at targeting small and marginal farmers who are in need of financial support.

Educational qualifications are not a prerequisite for applying to this scheme.

The application process is straightforward and designed to be user-friendly.

Interested beneficiaries must visit their local agricultural office to obtain the application form.

The application form can also be downloaded from the official government website.

Applicants are required to submit a copy of their Aadhaar card for identity verification.

Proof of land ownership is also necessary to establish eligibility.

Additionally, applicants must provide a bank account statement to facilitate the disbursement of funds.

Once the application is filled out and all necessary documents are gathered, it must be submitted to the local agricultural office.

The application will then be reviewed by the designated officials.

The approval process typically takes about 30 days from the date of submission.

Disbursement of funds is made directly to the beneficiary's bank account.

The funds are released in installments based on the completion of specific milestones.

The first installment is released upon approval of the application.

Subsequent installments are released after verification of the construction progress.

The scheme is implemented by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying under the Ministry of Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying.

This department is responsible for overseeing the implementation of various livestock-related welfare schemes.

Contact details for the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying can be found on the official government website.

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of sustainable practices in livestock management.

By providing proper shelter and access to water, the scheme aims to improve the health and productivity of livestock.

This, in turn, contributes to increased milk production and better income for farmers.

The scheme is expected to benefit not only individual farmers but also the rural economy as a whole.

Statistically, it is estimated that the implementation of this scheme could lead to a 20% increase in milk production in the targeted regions.

Furthermore, the scheme aligns with the government's broader goals of doubling farmers' income by 2022.

The initiative is part of the larger National Livestock Mission which was launched in 2014.

The National Livestock Mission aims to promote sustainable development of livestock sector through various interventions.

The Assistance for Cattleshed, Gaman, Water Tank and Bucket scheme is one of the key components of this mission.

The government has allocated a budget of ₹500 crore for the implementation of this scheme over the next five years.

This budget is aimed at ensuring that adequate resources are available for the successful rollout of the scheme.

The scheme has received positive feedback from beneficiaries in various states.

Farmers have reported improvements in livestock health and productivity after availing the benefits of the scheme.

Moreover, the scheme has also contributed to better water management practices among farmers.

By encouraging the construction of water tanks, the scheme helps in conserving water resources.

This is particularly important in regions facing water scarcity.

The scheme also aims to promote gender equality by encouraging women farmers to participate in livestock management.

Women play a crucial role in the dairy sector and their involvement is vital for the success of this initiative.

The government has also organized awareness programs to educate farmers about the benefits of the scheme.

These programs are conducted in collaboration with local NGOs and agricultural extension services.

The Assistance for Cattleshed, Gaman, Water Tank and Bucket scheme represents a significant step towards improving the livelihoods of rural farmers.

It provides them with the necessary resources to enhance their agricultural practices and ensure the welfare of their livestock.

The scheme is an example of the government's commitment to supporting the agricultural sector.

It reflects the broader vision of promoting sustainable rural development in India.

Overall, the Assistance for Cattleshed, Gaman, Water Tank and Bucket scheme is a comprehensive initiative that addresses multiple aspects of livestock management.

It provides essential financial support while promoting sustainable practices and improving the overall quality of life for farmers.
